Card: The left ventricle is the heart's main pump. It pushes oxygen-rich blood through the aortic valve into the aorta and out to the whole body. It also forms the heart's tip, the apex.

Connections:
- Left atrium: Mitral valve (receives oxygen-rich blood)
- Aorta: Aortic valve (pumps blood out to the whole body)
- Interventricular septum: shared wall (separates it from the right ventricle)
- Papillary muscles: attached to its inner wall (they hold the mitral valve flaps)
- Left anterior descending artery (LAD): runs over its front (with the diagonal and marginal branches, its blood supply)
Conditions:
- Heart failure: the muscle becomes too weak or too stiff to pump enough blood; people feel tired and short of breath.
- Left ventricular hypertrophy: the wall thickens after years of high blood pressure.
- Heart attack (myocardial infarction): part of the muscle dies when a coronary artery is blocked; the left ventricle is the area most often affected.
- Cardiomyopathy: diseases of the heart muscle itself, some inherited.
Notes:
- Its wall is about three times thicker than the right ventricle’s because it pumps blood around the whole body.
